title: Piemonte's Diesel Rollercoaster: A Sharp Drop, a Steady Climb Back
dek: While Benzina creeps quietly higher, Gasolio in Piemonte is four days into recovering from a sudden late-July plunge.
body: In Piemonte, self-service Benzina is running at €2.0094/L today, just 0.13 cents below the national self-service average of €2.0107/L — essentially in line with the rest of Italy. Gasolio tells a similar story at €2.1166/L, sitting about 0.7 cents under the national figure of €2.1236/L, keeping the region a touch cheaper than average at the pump for both fuels.

The two fuels have moved very differently this past week. Benzina has crept up steadily for six straight days, from €1.9921 to €2.0094/L (+0.87%), a slow but uninterrupted climb. Gasolio, by contrast, plunged from €2.1911 to €2.0791/L in a single day on July 29 — a 5.1% drop — before starting a steady four-day recovery back up to today's €2.1166/L. Piemonte's station network stayed essentially unchanged through all of it: 1,846 registered stations with 1,686 reporting prices today (91.3%), down just one station from yesterday, a sign the local network is stable even as prices swing.

Catching a single-day 5% diesel move and then tracking its recovery day-by-day, for one specific region out of twenty, is the kind of detail a manually-updated spreadsheet would never keep up with. Fuel Dashboard rebuilds itself every morning from the national MIMIT feed — no analyst re-typing numbers, no stale exports — because it was built with Claude Code to run the whole pipeline autonomously.

caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Piemonte, where diesel just lived through a wild week. Self-service Gasolio plunged 5.1% in a single day on July 29, then spent four straight days climbing back — while Benzina quietly crept up 0.87% over the same week. Both fuels are still running slightly below Italy's national self-service average.

Fuel Dashboard is a free, self-updating site tracking petrol and diesel prices across all 20 Italian regions, refreshed every morning straight from the MIMIT national feed. No spreadsheet, no manual re-entry — just a pipeline that pulls the data, picks a different region to spotlight each day, and republishes itself automatically. Take a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

The part I keep coming back to: this entire thing — data ingestion, daily region rotation, article writing, site rebuild — runs end-to-end with Claude Code. A few years ago this would've been a recurring manual task or a small dev project. Now it's a standing automation that just... works, every morning, without anyone opening Excel. That's the real story here as much as the fuel prices are.
